title: Treating SQL as a Procedural Language
pattern: Performing multiple sequential database queries to iteratively update records row-by-row instead of using set-based SQL operations.
why_bad: It causes extremely high network latency. The database performs individual transactional writes and index updates per row instead of batching them in a single query.
detection: SQL update/insert queries executing inside procedural loops over loaded primary keys.
counterexample: Executing targeted updates in an asynchronous queue handler where batching is impossible.
fix: Rewrite the query as a single, set-based operation (e.g. `UPDATE users SET status = 'Inactive' WHERE id IN (...)`).
